sentences.text: Dyoplosaurus is a single-species genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur belonging to the Ankylosaurinae subfamily, known from fossils found in Alberta.
The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, measured roughly 4 to 4.5 meters in length, stood 1.7 meters wide, and possessed a skull 35 centimeters across.
Like most members of its family, this quadrupedal herbivore was a terrestrial animal with an armored body and a bony club at the end of its tail.
Its scientific name translates to 'double-armoured lizard' and 'sharp-scaled', reflecting the Greek and Latin roots used by its original describers.
Researchers suggest that the small tail club implies these knobs were not primarily defensive weapons.
The holotype specimen was collected in 1919 from the lower ten meters of the Dinosaur Park Formation near the Red Deer River in Alberta, Canada.
Evgeny Maleev named a second species, D. giganteus, in 1956 based on fossils from Mongolia.
Walter Coombs synonymized Dyoplosaurus with Euoplocephalus in 1971, establishing that it had been incorrectly included in that genus.
However, a 2009 re-description by Arbour, Burns, and Sissons argued that Dyoplosaurus is a valid taxon, a conclusion affirmed in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.
The time range for Dyoplosaurus is recorded as Campanian to Campanian, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
It coexisted with Edmontonia, Euoplocephalus, Scolosaurus, Chasmosaurus, Corythosaurus, Gryposaurus, Parasaurolophus, Gorgosaurus, Hesperonychus, Latenivenatrix, Caenagnathus, and Chirostenotes.
A 2014 study suggested that D. giganteus is a nomen dubium because its defining traits are found in all ankylosaurines.
